outputs.block:2:text:0: VIPs went art-hunting at Frieze Art Fair and I went looking for people under 30 who buy art. As it turns out, they’re an elusive bunch, which is not what you’d expect given the headlines generated by Clare McAndrew ’s Art Basel and UBS Survey of Global Collecting 2026, released last week. 根据一项调查的 3,100 收藏家, Gen Z makes up the biggest spending demographic in the art market. It was a deus ex machina for the art world, which has been hungrily hunting
outputs.block:2:text:1: for a new horizon for years, eager to future-proof itself. First it was the promise of an exploding Asian market, then of digital art and NFTs, and of the Middle East. Now, Gen Z have been tasked with its rebooting. 首先,它是亚洲市场爆炸的承诺,然后是数字艺术和NFTs,以及中东。
outputs.block:3:text:0: 但—如我的高中经济学老师告诉我们—统计数据比科学更有艺术。数据是可图的;你可以做你想要的理性内。The yearning to render something as wide as the art world empirical is one-part helpful, two-part silly. (“多种现实可以在同一分钟内存在,同一时刻,一个站起来,”如一个经销商告诉我在新鲜 .) 关于“情绪”的任何报告都是勇敢的,但可错误的捕捉。 300 多可能有经验。
outputs.block:3:text:1: 在伦敦的白色大帐篷里,一个阳光明媚的星期三。
outputs.block:4:text:0: You’ve already read all about it : In 2025, Gen Z(出生于1997年至2012年) spent ⁇  three times the survey-wide average of $124,265 by older generations. The report concedes that its sample size is specific and small: 279 of the 3,100 respondents were themselves Gen Z. Around 15 of them made up ⁇  half of the approximately 31 respondents who bought a work priced above $1 million in 2025 and the first half of 2026. 该报告认为其样品尺寸是具体和小: 279 的 3,100 位受访者是自己 Gen Z. 约 15 的受访者占据了近一半的约 31 位受访者谁购买了一份工作价格超过 $1 百万在2025年和2026年上半年。
outputs.block:5:text:0: 在Niru Ratnam在Fitzrovia,Tim Schneider,Georgina Adam,和Ratnam主办了一次关于下一代收藏家的谈话:“这个人口有更少的愿望,以便他们能够购买绘画,”Sneider说,同时也喷水冷水的希望,这个世代(谁,我应该添加,仍然很大程度上年龄17至25岁)将做他们的老年人。
outputs.block:5:text:1: “在市场的一些部分之间,他们相信这笔钱会清洁地转移到下方,并且他们会用它购买艺术,”继续切纳德, “这是一个很远的陷阱。 20 -something visitors trickled in late to the talk and took notes. One of them, sitting a row in front of me, giggled when the topic of Gen Z screen time habits came up. 他们中的一位,坐在我面前,在我面前,在我面前,在我面前,在我面前。

outputs.block:8:text:0: “Bullshit,” said one dealer in the Focus section, the part of the fair for emerging artists. “The profession is aging so quickly,” he added, noting that the vast majority of his collector base is now 50 and up. Four dealer told me that interfamilial collecting is quite a thing—but it makes it hard to say who’s spending, and where the work is hanging. A daughter may pick out a work, but mom may pay for it. So, who is the collector?
outputs.block:9:text:0: “你很兴奋,当你有一个或两个基因Z买家,”一个奥地利经销商说,“如果他们存在,他们在亚洲,”另一个 echoed。
outputs.block:10:text:0: 我们千禧一代,现在大约30～45岁,可以记住一个流动和有趣,低利率艺术市场。 That’s when the bulk of us entered the workforce in this industry. Younger professionals are working under no delusions now, having likely missed much of that era, and having started their careers in a pandemic-leveled, locked down, high-利率经济。
outputs.block:11:text:0: “在报告中所说的是事实上发生的事情的相反,”一个经销商说,“如果从调查中任何东西都是真实的,那就是Gen Z收藏家在口味方面跟随他们的父母,在历史上有价值的艺术方面,但我不再看到实验和信任的空间。
outputs.block:11:text:1: 年轻收藏家不信任这个系统,他们对自己的钱更关心。
outputs.block:12:text:0: 因此,Gen Z: not yet officially trending—at least not along the aisles I wandered down. But, age is nothing but a number, and as we in the art business know well, numbers can be fudged。
